Disjoint Paths on Planar Graphs
In this paper, we study the Planar Disjoint Paths problem: Given an undirected planar graph with n vertices and a set of k pairs of vertices, the goal is to find a set k pairwise vertex-disjoint paths connecting each pairs.
We present an FPT-algorithm for the Planar Disjoint Paths problem which takes linear time depends on n and single exponential time depends on k. This improves the two previously best-known algorithms: linear in n time but double exponential in k time algorithm [Discrete Applied Mathematics 1995] and single exponential in k but n to the 6 time algorithm [STOC 2020].
FVS on Unit Disk Graphs
Given an undirected graph, the FVS(Feedback Vertex Set) problem asks for finding a minimum number of vertices whose removal makes the graph acyclic. We study this problem on unit disk graphs (UDGs). Disks in the plane forms a vertices of UDG, and two vertices are connected by an edge of UDG if their corresponding disks are intersect each other.
The FVS problem is NP-hard, but in the parametrized complexity theory, we analyze the running time of an algorithm with respect to the input size and a new parameter. Here, we use the solution size as a parameter.
In this work, we present an ETH-Tight algorithm for the FVS problem on unit disk graphs. In other words, if there is an algorithm faster than our algorithm, it disobeys ETH hypothesis, which is a stronger version of P!=NP hypothesis.
Random Geometric graphs
Geometric random graphs can be models for many real-world graphs. In this work, we focus on hyperbolic random graphs. A hyperbolic random graph can be considered as a mathematical model for analyzing scale-free networks since it effectively explains the power-law degree distribution of scale-free networks.
Using randomness and geometrical properties, various algorithms can be improved using average-case analysis. In this work, we present efficient algorithms for computing a maximum clique problem. We evaluate the performance of our algorithm theoretically and practically.
Distance Oracles for Geometric Graphs
In this work, we study approximate distance oracles for fault-tolerant geometric graphs. Given a geometric graph G, our goal is to design a data structure using linear space so that, given two query vertices and a set of failed vertices, an approximate distance between the two query vertices avoiding the failed vertices can be computed efficiently.
In general, no data structure for this problem using subquadratic space exists. In this work, using geometric tools, we presented a data structure for this problem on geometric graphs using near-linear space.

intro.text:
How do cells sense their world?

MEMBRANES · SENSORY RECEPTORS · AI

We explore how ion channels force, temperature, and chemical signals—by connecting molecular structure, membrane environments, and function.

Research
Recreating membrane environments. Understanding sensory receptors.

How does a cell detect heat, a chemical signal, or a mechanical force? Sensory receptors connect these stimuli to cellular responses. Ion channels do so by controlling the movement of ions across a membrane.

At Kwon Lab, a central goal is to quantitatively recreate the membrane environments in which sensory receptors operate. We seek to control and measure lipid composition, bilayer properties, geometry, and electrochemical conditions, then determine how thesevariables influence molecular structure, regulation, and function.

Mechanosensing is one part of this broader effort. We also investigate thermal and chemical activation, molecular interactions, and disease-related changes. By combining cryo-EM, membrane reconstitution, biochemistry, functional measurements, and AI-guided approaches, we connect defined membrane conditions to testable molecular mechanisms.

Membranes shape the environment in which sensory receptors work. Conceptual illustration; not an experimentally determined molecular structure.

TRPV1 · Heat & chemical sensing

How do temperature and a chemical stimulus work together to open an ion channel? This capsaicin-bound TRPV1 structure illustrates the molecular architecture behind sensory activation.

Kwon et al., Nature Structural & Molecular Biology (2021). PDB 7LPE · Rat TRPV1, capsaicin-bound, 48 °C, open-state class 1.ChimeraX rendering of experimental coordinates. Cutaway membrane is schematic with approximate placement. Protein rotation is for viewing, not simulated molecular motion.

TRPV4–RhoA · Molecular regulation

How do sensory channels integrate environmental cues with regulation inside the cell? This TRPV4–RhoA complex highlights the molecular interface linking channel gating, cellular regulation, and disease.

Kwon et al., Nature Communications (2023). PDB 8FC7 · Human TRPV4–RhoA with antagonist GSK2798745. RhoA is shown in green on the cytoplasmic side.Icons summarize stimuli and modulators; responses can involve context-dependent cellular pathways. They do not depict activation of this antagonist-bound structure. The cutaway membrane is schematic. Rotation is for structural viewing, not a molecular-dynamics simulation.

Research themes

01 · Quantitatively recreating membrane environments

How can we reproduce the membrane conditions that shape receptor behavior—and measure how faithfully those conditions are recreated? We develop experimentally defined membrane systems to examine how lipid composition, bilayer organization, geometry, and electrochemical conditions influence sensory receptor structure, regulation, and activity. Mechanosensing is one application of this framework, alongside thermal and chemical activation and molecular modulation.

We are developing and comparing reconstitution strategies using proteoliposomes, nanodiscs, and native-lipid particles, while exploring polymer-based vesicles as complementary platforms. These systems offer different opportunities to control lipid composition, bilayer organization, curvature, and compartmentalization. Membrane tension, curvature, thickness, and electrical potential are distinct variables: we seek to characterize them independently wherever possible rather than treating any one of them as a proxy for the others.

A central goal is to connect controlled changes in the membrane environment with cryo-EM analysis and functional measurements. Compartmentalized systems also offer a route toward defined ionic gradients and membrane potentials, provided these conditions are measured and maintained. This work invites collaboration with membrane biophysicists, polymer chemists, materials scientists, and specialists in quantitative membrane characterization.

02 · Revealing how sensory receptors change state

Sensory ion channels convert thermal, chemical, and mechanical inputs into changes in ion flow. We investigate how stimulus recognition is coupled to opening, closing, and regulation, and how these processes depend on the membrane and associated proteins. By comparing structures across defined ligand and membrane conditions, we aim to identify the interactions that stabilize different conformations.

Cryo-EM provides structural snapshots; biochemical and electrophysiological experiments test their functional meaning. We use this combination to evaluate candidate gating mechanisms, distinguish ligand recognition from downstream activation, and understand how disease-associated changes disrupt regulation. A structure obtained under one preparation condition is not assumed to represent the dominant physiological state.

03 · Understanding channels as molecular assemblies

Many channels function as assemblies of several subunits, and some combine distinct subunit types. We study how composition, stoichiometry, and subunit interfaces influence assembly, stimulus sensitivity, ion conduction, and pharmacological responses. Regulatory proteins can provide an additional layer of control by coupling cellular signals to channel conformation.

Our approach connects co-expression and biochemical isolation of defined complexes with structural analysis and functional comparison. The goal is to explain properties that emerge from the assembled complex and cannot be predicted simply by adding together the behavior of its individual components. We are interested in collaborations that link molecular assemblies to cellular physiology.

04 · Discovering molecules that tune receptor function

Small molecules, lipids, peptides, toxins, and regulatory proteins can alter channel activity through direct binding, changes in the surrounding membrane, or both. We investigate where these modulators act, which conformational states they favor, and how binding is coupled to a functional response.

Together with chemistry and pharmacology collaborators, we aim to connect molecular modifications with changes in potency, efficacy, selectivity, and state dependence. We are also interested in whether chemical changes can switch the direction of modulation—for example, from inhibition to activation. Binding affinity and functional effect are evaluated separately: a strong predicted or measured interaction does not by itself establish how a channel will respond.

05 · Connecting AI predictions to experiments

We use AI-assisted approaches to generate and prioritize hypotheses about sensory receptors. Research directions include structural modeling of protein complexes, analysis of candidate interaction surfaces, prioritization of small molecules or peptides, and selection of mutations that can discriminate between competing mechanisms. We are particularly interested in accounting for alternative protein conformations and membrane context when interpreting predictions.

Predict → Design → Test → Refine. Candidate interactions are tested through protein preparation, biochemical assays, functional measurements, and structural analysis as appropriate. Agreement and disagreement between prediction and experiment both guide the next iteration. We welcome collaborations with computational groups that want to evaluate their methods against experimentally tractable membrane-protein systems.

06 · Building a shared path from mechanism to application

Our long-term aim is to make membrane-protein mechanisms useful for understanding disease and guiding molecular intervention. Connections to chemical probes, therapeutic discovery, protein engineering, synthetic biology, biosensors, and biomaterials grow from this mechanistic foundation. For students, these projects offer multiple entry points—from making and testing proteins to analyzing structures and designing computational hypotheses.

Our Approach & Why it matters
See the structure. Measure the function. Explain the mechanism.

Build: Purify membrane proteins and reconstitute them into defined membrane systems.
Visualize: Use cryo-EM and complementary structural approaches, including cryo-ET where appropriate, to examine molecular organization and conformational states.
Measure: Connect structures to electrophysiology and quantitative biochemical and biophysical assays.
Predict and test: Use AI-guided structural and interaction analysis to generate hypotheses, then challenge them experimentally.

For students: one question, many ways to explore it

Could changing the membrane make a channel easier to open? Could a mutation change its response to heat? Could an AI-predicted interaction reveal a new regulator? Students can approach these questions through computation, protein preparation, membrane experiments, and structural analysis—learning how different kinds of evidence fit together.

For collaborators: connecting disciplines across borders

We welcome collaborations in membrane biophysics, polymer and materials chemistry, sensory biology, electrophysiology, AI, and chemical discovery. We are especially interested in combining well-defined membrane environments with structural and functional measurements.

Our broader interests connect molecular mechanisms to disease, host–pathogen interactions, therapeutic discovery, protein engineering, synthetic biology, biosensors, and biomaterials.

Drone Group
DRONE GROUP - OVERVIEW
E-mail : yoopata@postech.ac.kr
"We aims to develop fully autonomous palm-sized drones for industrial and military applications by combining a variety of the state-of-the-art control and sensing technologies."
- Indoor navigation system
- UAV system design
- Multi-agent control
- DRL based UAV control
1. Navigation system
The development of navigation system and sensor fusion algorithms is critical for the effective control of drones in both indoor and outdoor environments. Our approach integrates optical motion capture systems for precise indoor navigation and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) for accurate outdoor positioning, ensuring reliable and consistent performance.
2. UAV system design
Multirotor system is widely used in variety of aerial missions. To find a suitable set of multirotor hardware for each mission, an optimization based design method is developed which maximize flight time under flight scenario of the mission.
3. Control algorithm
Recently, quadrotors are required to be more robust and agile for application to sophisticated flights and tasks in confined and complex places. According to those demands, we are developing control algorithms for both single and multi-agent drone systems.
4. AI-based UAV/UGV control
Plant control using reinforcement learning is one of the most prominent control methods these days. The sim2real transfer algorithm, which transfers the policies learned in simulation to actual systems, is a core technology in this field. To ensure more robust and precise control performance, we are researching SIM2REAL algorithms and validating them using drone systems.

AI GROUP - OVERVIEW
E-mail : jjongs [at] postech.ac.kr
"Utilizing the power of artificial intelligence, we aim to address complex problems across diverse domains, ultimately benefiting humanity."
- AI-based control
- Applicable RL algorithms

SLAM Group
SLAM GROUP - OVERVIEW
E-mail : cwonpark@postech.ac.kr
"Our group focuses on pioneering research to enhance SLAM, hardware, autonomous driving, and 3D reconstruction with the goal of developing advanced technologies that enhance the safety, efficiency, and dependability of autonomous system."
- Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
- Hardware development
- Autonomous driving
- 3D reconstruction
1. Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
SLAM is a computational challenge that enables robots or autonomous vehicles to map and navigate unknown environments simultaneously using sensor data such as cameras, lidars, or radars. Our research focuses on sensor fusion for SLAM technology, which involves integrating lidar data with other sensor data to produce more accurate maps and enable more reliable navigation.
2. Hardware development
We have constructed hardware components and sensor modules in order to conduct research and practical experiments on SLAM applications. We have developed a sensor module for logging LiDAR and IMU data, as well as a sensor module for integrating various sensors such as radar, camera, and IMU.
3. Autonomous driving
Beyond our SLAM research, we are applying our findings to the development of autonomous driving systems. By utilizing the map, estimated robot pose, and path planning algorithms, we are creating mobile autonomous driving solutions for various environments and purposes, leveraging the advanced capabilities of SLAM technology.
4. 3D Reconstruction
3D reconstruction is the process of creating a digital 3D model of an object or scene using computer vision and graphics techniques, such as SLAM. Our research aims to implement an automatic scanning system for 3D reconstruction using robots, leveraging SLAM technology to recover the 3D geometry and appearance of objects and scenes from 2D images or point clouds in an automated and efficient manner.

Energy Group
ENERGY GROUP - OVERVIEW
E-mail : junheemike@postech.ac.kr
"At the forefront of battery informatics, our group is pioneering novel approaches for analysis, diagnosis, and prognosis of rechargeable batteries to ensure their efficient and safe usage."
- Model development
- System identification
- Aging diagnosis
- Optimal scheduling
1. Model development
Mathematical models are milestone for battery informatics, so we are trying to develop an advanced model for lithium-ion batteries.
We develop meso- and micro-scopic electrochemical models as well as continuum scale models. Using them, we mainly conduct morphological analysis such as investigating of battery performance or degradation affected by morphological features. Also, an analytic steady state model is used to prove other numerical models.
2. System identification
Battery system(or state) identification is a necessary step to practically use the models, which is an optimization to match our models to target real batteries. In general, this process includes solving a highly nonlinear and complex problem, which requires a very expensive computational cost and is hard to obtain an accurate solution. Thus, we are trying to improve optimization algorithms for that in novel ways.
3. Aging diagnosis
Battery diagnosis is crucial to ensure battery safety. We develop advanced battery aging estimation algorithm using empirical models, electrochemical models, and neural networks. Further, we are trying to improve aging estimation by reflecting several degradation phenomena, e.g., particle cracking, lithium plating, and so on.
4. Optimal scheduling
Based on battery model and state estimation, we design optimal control methods. Specifically, we control input current to decrease battery degradation or improve state estimation. For this, we usually exploit reinforcement learning.

intro.text:
Understanding how the brain can generate
flexible behavior
We study the neural mechanisms underlying
higher cognitive function. By using state-of-
the-art technologies, we investigate how the
brain can learn and compute such flexible behavior.

Building efficient Brain-Machine Interface
We develop an efficient information
communication algorithm using the neural
interface to study flexible learning and cognitive control.

Technologies for neuroscience
Our work involves studying complex behavior in
mice, using the next-generation tools such as
Neuropixels neural probes, Calcium-imaging,
Rodent Virtual Reality System, Optogenetics,
and ultrafast Brain-Machine Interface.

We are currently recruiting talented graduate students and postdocs!
Undergraduate students who are interested in immersing themselves
in the field of systems neuroscience are also welcome.

The brain has evolved to control a complex biological device: the body. It is so flexible and adaptive that our brain can learn to control other devices and communicate with other agents through our body. By leveraging this remarkable nature of the brain, brain-machine interface (BMI) tries to provide a direct link between a brain and a machine for control and communication. BMI has great potential for the restoration of sensory and motor function to help patients with peripheral neuropathy, spinal cord injury, stroke, or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

Recent advances in neuroscience, machine learning, and technology have contributed to improvements in the speed and accuracy of brain-machine interface (BMI) communication. However, several limitations still exist for its practical use.

1. Neural recording quality: While there have been improvements, the stability of neural recordings can still be a challenge, often requiring frequent recalibration of the decoder. This is because neural signals can vary over time due to factors such as electrode drift or changes in brain activity patterns.

2. Dynamic nature of neural representations: Research has shown that neural representations for sensory, motor, and abstract information can change over time. This raises questions about the feasibility of traditional decoding-based approaches, which rely on stable neural representations. Adapting BMI systems to account for these dynamic changes is an active area of research.

3. Decoding novel or unexperienced objects: The brain lacks neural representations for previously unexperienced or novel objects, making it impossible to decode these representations. While it is true that decoding novel objects can be challenging, recent research has explored methods such as transfer learning or generative models to address this limitation and improve decoding accuracy.

4. For individuals who have experienced stroke and lost function in their motor cortex, it can be challenging to find motor representations in other areas of the brain. We need to train alternative brain regions to control motor functions.

5. Limited channel count: Most commonly used neural probes still have a relatively low channel count, which can limit the amount of information that can be extracted from the brain. However, advancements in electrode technology are being pursued to increase channel counts and enable more comprehensive neural recordings.
Therefore, we need to step back and take a different approach, rather than finding the neural representation, but instead integrate these representations into the neural circuit. Our lab aims to build an efficient protocol to communicate with the brain for practical BMI.

Our lab conducts research that are contributing to the treatment of cancer by understanding the altered metabolic behaviors of cancer cells and identifying vital metabolic mechanisms for cancer growth and survival. The understanding of tumor metabolism has gained significant attention and has become the hallmark of cancer in recent decades. However, previous metabolic studies focused on cancer cells have had limitations due to the insufficient consideration of the tumor’s growing environment.
1. Our research team aims to analyze and elucidate the metabolic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) using cutting-edge technologies and ideas.
2. We observe how various types of cancer adapt to their unique metabolic environments through multi-omics approaches.
3. We further investigate key metabolic mechanisms required for tumor growth and survival in the context of in vivo using state-of-the-art genetically engineered mouse and surgical mouse models, and fresh tissue samples from cancer patients.
Our research encompasses the development of therapies, starting from fundamental research to assess whether these key metabolic mechanisms can be utilized as treatment targets.

Cancer Metabolism
In vivo Metabolic Vulnerability
Solid tumors grow and survive within a nutrient-restricted tumor microenvironment (TME) shaped by abnormal vascular architecture and fibrosis. Under these conditions, cancer cells activate diverse metabolic pathways to sustain proliferation and survival. However, most conventional metabolic studies have been conducted under nutrient-rich in vitro conditions, which inadequately capture the metabolic composition of the in vivo TME. As a result, many metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies that showed promise in preclinical studies have repeatedly failed to demonstrate the expected efficacy in clinical trials.
To overcome these limitations, our laboratory aims to reconstruct metabolic conditions that more faithfully reflect the actual tumor environment by leveraging quantitative metabolomics data obtained directly from in vivo tumor tissues. Using this platform, we will systematically investigate how cancer cells rewire and adapt their intracellular metabolic networks under nutrient-limited conditions.
Through this approach, we seek to precisely characterize intracellular metabolic alterations of cancer cells in vivo, analyze the relationship between TME metabolite availability and intracellular metabolite states, and identify the metabolic pathways that become activated. Building on these findings, we will uncover metabolic dependencies that are not apparent under standard culture conditions but are essential for cancer cell survival and proliferation in vivo. Ultimately, this study aims to define in vivo metabolic vulnerabilities of solid tumors and propose new metabolism-based therapeutic targets that are grounded in the physiological tumor microenvironment.
고형암은 비정상적 혈관 구조와 섬유화로 영양소가 제한된 종양 미세환경(tumor microenvironment, TME) 내에서 성장하고 생존합니다. 이러한 환경에서 암세포는 증식과 생존을 유지하기 위해 다양한 대사 경로를 활성화하지만, 기존의 대사 연구 대부분은 영양소(Key nutrinet)가 풍부한 in vitro 조건에 기반하고 있어 실제 TME의 대사 조성을 충분히 반영하지 못하는 한계가 있습니다. 이로 인한 한계로, 전임상 연구에서는 유망한 효과를 보였던 다수의 대사 타깃 치료 전략들이 임상 시험 단계에서 기대만큼의 치료 효과를 입증하지 못하고 실패하는 사례가 반복적으로 보고되어 왔습니다.
본 연구실은 이러한 한계를 극복하기 위해, in vivo 종양 조직으로부터 획득한 TME 대사체 정량 정보를 기반으로 이를 통해 실제 종양 환경을 반영한 대사 조건을 재현하고, 암세포가 제한된 영양 환경에서 어떻게 세포 내 대사체 네트워크를 재구성하며 적응하는지를 체계적으로 분석하고자 합니다.
이러한 접근법을 통해 in vivo 모델에서 암세포의 세포 내부 대사체 변화를 정밀하게 규명하고, TME 대사 조성과 세포 내부 대사체 간의 연관성을 분석, 활성화된 대사경로를 밝힙니다. 이를 기반으로, 기존 배양 조건에서는 드러나지 않지만 in vivo 환경에서 암세포의 생존(survival)과 증식(proliferation)에 필수적인 대사 의존성을 발굴하여, 궁극적으로 본 연구는 고형암의 in vivo metabolic vulnerability를 규명하고, 실제 종양 환경을 반영한 새로운 대사 기반 치료 타깃을 제시하는 것을 목표로 합니다.

Metastasis
Overcoming dynamic environmental change during metastasis
Cancer metastasis is a fatal disease in which cancer cells originating from a primary tumor migrate to distant organs and successfully establish secondary lesions (colonization), ultimately leading to patient mortality. During the metastatic process, primary tumor cells transition into circulating tumor cells (CTCs), thereby detaching from the primary tumor microenvironment.
As a consequence, cancer cells are simultaneously exposed to profound extrinsic changes associated with the bloodstream a drastically different environment and intrinsic alterations resulting from the loss of cell–matrix adhesion (detachment).
Subsequently, disseminated cancer cells must adapt to the distinct microenvironment of distant organs and achieve successful colonization to survive and proliferate. Throughout this process, cancer cells encounter diverse stresses, including elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS). To overcome these stresses or sustain proliferation, cancer cells have to exploit metabolites available in their surrounding environment.
However, most studies on cancer metastasis to date have primarily focused on transcriptomic study, while investigations centered on metabolic changes throughout the metastatic cascade remain relatively limited.
Therefore, our laboratory aims to systematically elucidate the metabolic adaptations underlying cancer metastasis using metabolomic approaches, with particular emphasis on two critical hurdles: the formation of circulating tumor cells and the subsequent colonization of distant organs.
암 전이는 원발암에서 유래한 암세포가 원격 장기로 이동하여 정착(colonization)함으로써 궁극적으로 환자의 사망에 이르게 하는 치명적인 질환입니다. 원발암 세포는 전이 과정 중 circulating tumor cell (CTC) 로 전환되며, 이 과정에서 지속적으로 증식해오던 원발암 미세환경에서 이탈하게 됩니다. 그 결과, 암세포는 혈액이라는 전혀 다른 extrinsic 환경 변화와 동시에 세포–기질 접착 상실(detachment)에 따른 intrinsic 변화를 동시에 경험하게 됩니다. 이후 전이된 암세포는 원격 장기라는 새로운 미세환경에 적응하고, 생존 및 증식을 위해 성공적인 colonization을 수행해야 합니다. 이 과정에서 암세포는 활성산소종(reactive oxygen species, ROS)과 같은 다양한 스트레스에 노출되며, 이를 극복하고 증식을 유지하기 위해 필연적으로 주변 환경의 대사체를 활용할 수밖에 없습니다.
그러나 지금까지의 암 전이 연구는 주로 전사체(transcriptome) 수준의 변화에 초점을 맞추어 이루어져 왔으며, 전이 과정 전반에서의 대사적(metabolic) 변화를 중심으로 한 연구는 상대적으로 제한적이었습니다.
이에 본 연구실은 암 전이 과정에서 주요한 장벽(hurdle)으로 작용하는 circulating tumor cell 형성 단계와 원격 장기에서의 colonization 단계를 metabolomics 연구를 통해 체계적으로 규명하고자 합니다.

T cell metabolism
Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, one of the immunotherapeutic approaches, has achieved unprecedented clinical success in hematological malignancies through antigen-specific recognition and potent cytotoxic activity. However, its efficacy in solid tumors remains limited. This limitation is attributed not only to antigen heterogeneity and physical barriers but also to the profoundly suppressive metabolic conditions of the tumor microenvironment (TME).
The tumor microenvironment is characterized by severe nutrient deprivation, hypoxia, acidosis, and the accumulation of immunosuppressive metabolites, all of which constrain the persistence and antitumor function of CAR-T cells. Following antigen recognition, CAR-T cells require rapid metabolic reprogramming to support robust proliferation and sustained effector functions. However, metabolic competition with tumor cells restricts access to essential nutrients, ultimately driving functional exhaustion of CAR-T cells.
Despite these challenges, most CAR-T–related studies to date have primarily focused on signaling pathways, gene expression, and the regulation of inhibitory immune receptors. In contrast, systematic analyses of the metabolic alterations experienced by CAR-T cells within the tumor microenvironment and their functional consequences remain relatively limited. Therefore, our laboratory aims to elucidate the key metabolic constraints encountered by CAR-T cells in the TME through metabolomics-based approaches and to develop metabolically enhanced next-generation CAR-T therapeutic strategies.
면역항암제 중 하나인 CAR-T 세포 치료는 항원 특이적 인식과 강력한 세포독성 기능을 통해 혈액암에서 획기적인 치료 성과를 이루었으나, 고형암에서는 여전히 제한적인 효능을 보이고 있습니다. 이는 항원 이질성이나 물리적 장벽뿐만 아니라, 종양이 형성하는 Tumor microenvironment, TME의 극심한 대사적 억제 조건과 밀접하게 관련되어 있습니다.
종양 미세환경은 영양소 고갈, 저산소증, 산성화, 그리고 면역 억제성 대사산물의 축적이라는 특징을 가지며, 이러한 환경은 CAR-T 세포의 지속성 및 항암 기능을 제한합니다. CAR-T 세포는 항원 인식 이후 빠른 증식과 지속적인 effector 기능 유지를 위해 급격한 대사 재편성을 요구받지만, 종양 세포와의 대사적 경쟁 속에서 필수 영양소의 이용이 제한되며 기능적 탈진(exhaustion)에 이르게 됩니다.
그러나 기존의 CAR-T 연구는 주로 신호전달, 유전자 발현, 면역억제 수용체 조절에 초점을 맞추어 왔으며, 종양 미세환경 전반에서 CAR-T 세포가 경험하는 대사적 변화와 그 기능적 결과를 체계적으로 분석한 연구는 상대적으로 부족한 실정입니다.
이에 본 연구실은 metabolomics를 통해 CAR-T 세포가 TME에서 직면하는 핵심 대사적 제약을 규명하고, 대사적으로 강화된 차세대 CAR-T 치료 전략을 개발하는 것을 목표로 합니다.

Research introduction

How cancer cells alter their metabolism and shape their distinctive metabolic milieu?, how cancer cells and other types of cell harness nutrients in their local environments (or Tumor MicroEnvironements, TMEs) for their benefits?, how systemic metabolism of the host affects TMEs and in turn influences the metabolism of cancer cells are major areas of focus in our lab.

The Lee lab conducts research that contributes to the treatment of cancer by understanding the altered metabolic behaviors of cancer cells and identifying vital metabolic mechanisms for cancer growth and survival.
The understanding of tumor metabolism has gained significant attention and has become the hallmark of cancer in recent decades. However, previous metabolic studies focused on cancer cells have had limitations due to the insufficient consideration of the tumor’s growing environment.

1. Our research team aims to analyze and elucidate the metabolic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) using cutting-edge technologies and ideas.
2. We observe how various types of cancer adapt to their unique metabolic environments through multi-omics approach and
3. further investigate key metabolic mechanisms required for tumor growth and survival in the context of in vivo using state-of-the-art genetically engineered mouse and surgical mouse models, and fresh tissue samples from cancer patients. Our research encompasses the development of therapies, starting from fundamental research to assess whether these key metabolic mechanisms can be utilized as treatment targets. The Lee lab eagerly awaits the support of motivated and curious students and researchers to work together in overcoming the unsolved challenges in the development of cancer treatments targeting metabolism.
학부생을 위한 실험실 소개

연구 내용

저희 연구실에서는 ‘암은 무엇을 먹고, 어떻게 사용하며 성장하는가?’에 관심이 있습니다. 사람이 생존을 위해 음식을 먹어야 하듯, 암이 성장 및 생존을 위해 반드시 사용해야하는 영양소와 대사 방식을 이해하고자 합니다. 이를 위해 암이 자라는 미세환경 (Tumor MicroEnvironment)의 대사 조성을 파악하고, 미세환경에서 일어나는 암세포와 다양한 세포 종들의 대사적 경쟁 및 협력 방식을 연구합니다. 궁극적으로는 암 성장 및 생존에 필수적인 대사 기능을 조절해 암세포를 굶겨 죽이는 새로운 개념의 항암 치료 개발을 목표로 하고 있습니다.

Keywords - Analog Integrated Circuit Design, Low Power IC Design, Mixed Signal IC Circuit Design, Power Management ICs: Switching Inductive/Capacitive DC-DC Converter, LDO Regulator, AC-DC Rectification, Power Electronics, Fully-Autonomous SoC Synthesis with Deep Learning, Display Driver IC for OLED/LCD Displays, Sensor-Interface and Readout IC, Energy Harvesting Circuits, Wireless Power Transfer
Energy-Efficient Analog IC Design
Topic 1: Energy-Efficient Analog Integrated Circuit (IC) Design represents the art of achieving high performance with the lowest possible power budget. Analog and mixed-signal circuits form the backbone of sensor interfaces, communication links, and power regulation blocks, making energy efficiency a decisive factor for modern portable and embedded systems. By leveraging advanced circuit techniques—such as optimized biasing, leakage suppression, and subthreshold operation—designers can dramatically extend battery lifetime while minimizing thermal constraints. This paradigm is especially vital for next-generation applications, including IoT nodes, biomedical implants, and self-powered energy-harvesting platforms, where ultra-low-power operation defines system success.
Power Management Integrated Circuit (PMIC)
Topic 2: Power management integrated circuits (power management ICs or PMICs or PMU as unit) are integrated circuits for power management. Although PMIC refers to a wide range of chips (or modules in system-on-a-chip devices), most include several DC/DC converters or their control part. A PMIC is often included in battery-operated devices such as mobile phones and portable media players to decrease the amount of space required.
Energy Harvesting IC (EHIC)
Topic 3: Energy harvesting (also known as power harvesting or energy scavenging or ambient power) is the process by which energy is derived from external sources (e.g., solar power, thermal energy, wind energy, salinity gradients, and kinetic energy, also known as ambient energy), captured, and stored for small, wireless autonomous devices, like those used in wearable electronics and wireless sensor networks.
Wireless Power Transfer (WPT)
Topic 4: Wireless power transfer (WPT), wireless power transmission, wireless energy transmission (WET), or electromagnetic power transfer is the transmission of electrical energy without wires as a physical link. In a wireless power transmission system, a transmitter device, driven by electric power from a power source, generates a time-varying electromagnetic field, which transmits power across space to a receiver device, which extracts power from the field and supplies it to an electrical load. The technology of wireless power transmission can eliminate the use of the wires and batteries, thus increasing the mobility, convenience, and safety of an electronic device for all users. Wireless power transfer is useful to power electrical devices where interconnecting wires are inconvenient, hazardous, or are not possible.

intro.text: 음파는 사람이 들을 수 있는 영역인 가청주파수 20~2만 헤르츠(Hz)에서는 음악이 된다. 음악은 정서에 긍정적 영향을 주고 마음을 치료하는 도구가 되기도 한다. 하지만 사람이 들을 수 없는 영역인 초음파도 사람을 치료할 수 있다. 초음파를 통해 인체를 영상화해서 볼 수도 있고 초음파가 내는 높은 에너지를 통해 병을 치료할 수도 있다.   IT융합공학과 김형함 교수가 이끄는 초음파공학연구실은 초음파로 들리지 않는 음악을 작곡하고 악기를 만들어 환자를 치료하는 데 쓴다. 전기신호를 음향신호로 바꿔주는 장치인 초음파 트랜스듀서를 설계하고 제작하는 기술을 개발한다. 트랜스듀서가 만든 초음파를 쓰는 의료용 초음파 영상과 치료 기술을 개발한다. 고주파 초음파를 집중시켜 세포를 잡는 음향 집게로 세포의 특성을 분석하기도 한다.   연구실은 자체 제작한 초음파 트랜스듀서로 영상과 치료를 한 번에 할 수 있는 시스템들을 다수 개발했다. 경동맥의 혈류를 관찰할 수 있는 인체 부착형 장비도 개발했다. 혈관 속에 흐르는 혈액을 초음파로 분석해 혈전을 관찰하고 적혈구의 운동상태를 파악하는 것도 가능하다. 수술을 마친 환자의 수술 부위에 장착하면 피가 원활히 흐르는지 관찰해 환자의 회복 속도도 예측할 수 있다.   초음파로 세포를 붙잡고 특성을 파악하는 고주파 음향집게 기술도 개발했다. 초음파를 물 속에서 집중하면 물에 담긴 세포를 포획하고 이리저리 움직이면서 압력을 가할 수 있다. 세포의 물리적 특성을 연구하면 다양한 분야에 활용할 수 있다. 예를 들어 암세포를 붙잡아 관찰함으로써 암세포가 다른 조직으로 얼마나 잘 이동할 수 있는지를 확인할 수 있다.   김 교수는 연구실의 장점으로 장치 설계 능력을 꼽는다. 아이디어를 갖고 있다면 쓰임새에 맞게 특별한 트랜스듀서를 설계하고 실제 제작할 수 있는 장비를 갖췄다. 연구실 누구나 이를 활용해 아이디어를 현실로 바꿀 수 있다. 연구실은 의료 진단에 쓰는 광학 장비와 초음파를 결합하기 위해 투명한 초음파 트랜스듀서를 개발하는 데 성공했다. 인체에 유해한 납을 쓰지 않는 트랜스듀서도 성과 중 하나다.   연구실은 실제 의료 현장에서 초음파가 어떻게 쓰일지를 가장 중점적으로 생각한다. 세계 최고 수준의 초음파 트랜스듀서 연구센터를 구축하고 기술을 의료기기로 바꿔 실제 의료 현장에 제공하기 위해 오늘도 연구에 매진하고 있다.

Handling Real-World Data
While synthetically generated datasets have been widely used for training neural networks for image restoration, such networks do not perform well on real-world images due to the significant domain gap between naively synthesized datasets and real-world degradations. To better handle real-world degraded images, we have explored different possibilities such as real-world datasets and realistic degradation synthesis. Our RealBlur dataset, which is a dataset consisting of real-world blurred images and their ground-truth sharp images, is now utilized as a standard benchmark dataset by numerous works.

Camera ISPs
Camera ISPs produce visually-pleasing images from RAW data captured by camera sensors. Specifically, camera ISPs perform two tasks: image restoration and enhancement. The goals of our research are twofold. 1) We aim at accurate modeling of real-world camera ISPs so that we can more accurately model real-world image degradations. 2) We aim at replacing traditional camera ISPs with learnable ISPs for higher-quality imaging.

Beyond Single Images
Traditional image restoration tasks mainly focus on restoring a single image that is already captured by using a single camera. On the other hand, recent smartphones provide more than one cameras and additional sensors such as gyro sensors. Moreover, we may also program the way to capture images such as modulating the exposure time. We seek to exploit such possibilities.

RESEARCH CENTER
SCIENTIFIC MISSION
The primary goal of our research is to develop theory, algorithm, and system for visual computing. Specifically, we focus on creating and enhancing visual contents, reconstructing scene geometry and reflectance, and modeling light transport. To this end, we conduct interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computer graphics, computer vision, machine learning, and optics.
View Publications
Contact Lab
3D Reconstruction
We develop algorithms and systems to reconstruct our real world's 3D geometry and appearance. We can use the acquired 3D assets for diverse applications where we need to understand the 3D world.
Computational Imaging
We jointly develop theories, algorithms, and systems to achieve a superhuman vision in the form of new imaging and display systems.
Visual Synthesis
We develop algorithms that can synthesize new visual data with machine creativity.
Computational Photography
We develop algorithms to acquire the highest-quality visual data with existing imaging devices.

intro.text:
Current Research Topics
Surface/Interfacial Engineering: Smart Surfaces & Interfaces

Smart materials such as shape memory polymers (SMPs) offer significant potential for integration with biomimetic design strategies to create synthetic surfaces with diverse functionalities, including adhesion, wetting, and optical control. Our group has been exploring the bioinspired design of micro/nanostructured SMP and composite surfaces that exhibit reversible dry adhesion, tunable wetting, and adaptive light manipulation enabled by dynamically switchable structural and material properties.

Surface/Interfacial Engineering: Double-sided Processing on Ultrathin Si (UTSi) films

We propose a novel approach for double-sided semiconductor processing on ultrathin (<10 μm) silicon (UTSi) using self-delamination interfaces. Double-sided device fabrication offers significant advantages by increasing device density and enabling distinct functionalities on the front and back surfaces. This approach provides a new pathway toward next-generation semiconductor manufacturing and flexible electronics.

Micromanufacturing: Transfer Printing-based Microassembly

Transfer printing, which relies on switchable adhesion to polymer stamps, is a powerful technique for the deterministic assembly of micro- and nanomaterials into spatially organized, functional architectures in both two and three dimensions. Our group focuses on developing transfer printing-based manufacturing technologies for advanced semiconductor, display, and MEMS platforms, with applications in semiconductor packaging, micro-LED integration, and 3D MEMS assembly.

Device Engineering: Flexible Sensors and Energy Harvesters

Building on our manufacturing expertise, our group develops flexible electronic devices for energy harvesting and motion sensing through innovative design, fabrication, and optimization.

raw.name: 극저온 양자기체 연구실 (ULTRACOLD QUANTUM GASES PARK GROUP)

intro.text:
Strongly correlated physics with ultracold gases of polar molecules
We aim to produce quantum gases of bosonic and fermionic NaK molecules cooled to nanoKelvin (nK) temperatures - more than a million times colder than interstellar space. At these temperatures, the molecules' strong, long-range, anisotropic electric-dipole interactions dominate their many-body behavior, taking us far beyond the short-range contact interactions familiar from neutral atom experiments.
In the bulk, these dipolar forces can drive striking collective phenomena, including supersolids, dipolar quantum crystals, and p-wave topological superfluids. By incorporating an optical lattice and a high-NA microscope objective, we will pin the molecules in a crystal of light and image every site individually. This capability will allow us to engineer extended Hubbard and dipolar spin Hamiltonians, track correlations, and explore quantum phases that have so far remained purely theoretical.
Quantum computing with polar molecules in tweezer arrays
In this experiment, we assemble individual KCs molecules in tightly focused optical tweezers, arranging them like pixels in a two-dimensional grid. Each molecule's hyperfine levels will serve as qubits with seconds-long coherence times, while microwave or static electric fields can be applied to switch on dipolar interactions at will, enabling efficient and stable two-qubit gates via dipolar exchange.
Using a programmable tweezer array, we can re-position any pair of molecules on demand, achieving the flexible connectivity required for complex quantum algorithms and quantum error-correction codes. Moreover, the molecules' rich internal structure supports multilevel (qudit) encodings, allowing more efficient use of quantum resources as the processor scales from tens to thousands of sites.
Other research interests:
strongly interacting atomic gases and mixtures
Beyond molecules, we investigate ultracold atoms in the strongly interacting regime - where the scattering length between atoms rivals or even exceeds the mean interparticle spacing, pushing the system to the unitary limit. Using magnetic Feshbach resonances, we precisely tune interactions from weak to resonant and explore phenomena such as Fermi and Bose polarons, where a single impurity dresses itself with excitations of the quantum bath, and collective modes and vortex formation, which reveal non-equilibrium many-body dynamics in strongly correlated fluids.

intro.text:
RNA-binding protein
체관 발달을 관장하는 RNA 결합 단백질과 RNA 비암호화 부위 상호작용
1. 식물 발달 과정에서 전사 후 조절 및 번역 과정 조절
생명 현상은 DNA, RNA, 단백질 등의 다층적 수준에서 조절된다
최근 유전 정보가 생물학적 기능을 수행하는 단백질로 전달됨에 있어 전사 후 조절 과정, 선별적 번역 과정과 번역 효율의 조절이 RNA 염기 서열에 내재되어 있음이 알려지고 있다.
RNA가 단순히 단백질을 암호화 하는 것 뿐 아니라, 직접적으로 유전 정보의 발현을 조절하고 있음이 다양한 수준의 전사 후 조절 과정을 통해 이루어지고 있음이 밝혀지고 있으며, 이러한 일련의 RNA의 전사 후 조절 및 번역 조절 기능은 RNA의 대표적 비암호화 기능이며, RNA 결합 단백질과의 상호작용을 필수적으로 수반하고 있다.
하지만 대부분의 연구는 동물 및 질병 모델을 통해 이루어지고 있으며, 식물 발달 과정에서의 전사 후 조절 기작 및 선별적 번역 조절에 관한 연구는 매우 제한적으로 이루어지고 있다.
(그림1: 전사 후 및 번역 조절 과정 모식도)
2. 식물 에너지 분배 기관인 체관의 발달
식물에서의 에너지 수송 및 분배를 담당하는 체관 분화 및 발달 기작을 이해하기 위해서는 다양한 조절 기작의 시스템적 연구가 필요하며 새로운 전사 후 조절 인자로써의 RNA 결합 단백질의 발굴은 체관 발달 조절의 다층 조절 네트워크를 구축하기 위해 선행되어야 한다.
체관의 분화 과정은 다른 기관들의 분화 과정과는 달리 핵을 포함한 세포 소기관이 선택적으로 제거되는 과정을 수반하며, 전사인자들에 의한 유전자 발현 조절 이후에 수반되는 독립적 조절과정을 필요로 하지만 알려진 바는 전무하다.
체관 내에서 탄소 화합물 이외에 다양한 단백질, RNA들이 이동하고 있음이 알려져 있으며, 이들이 세포 간 정보 교환 및 식물 발달 과정에 기능을 수행할 것이라는 보고가 있어 왔다. 이는 RNA의 다층적 정보가 식물 고유의 발달 및 생존 프로그램에 중요하게 관여하고 있음을 의미한다.
(그림2: 체관을 통한 에너지 분배 제어 개념도)
3. 체관 발달을 관장하는 RNA 결합 단백질과 RNA 비암호화 부위 상호작용
본 연구는 식물 줄기세포로부터 에너지 수송 기관으로의 분화 과정을 모델로 사용하여
1. RNA가 지닌 비암호화 부위의 숨겨진 정보가 어떻게 RNA 결합 단백질에 의해 취합되고,
2. 필요한 에너지를 각 세포로 분배하기 위해 전달되며 해독되어 에너지 수송 기관의 발달을 조절하는지를 이해하고,
3. 이를 바탕으로 다세포 생물체에서 RNA 결합 단백질-RNA 비암호화 부위의 상호작용이 지닌 다양하고 특이적인 생물학적 정보를 규명하고자 한다.
(그림3: 체관 발달 과정에서의 RNA 결합 단백질에 의한 전사 후 조절 과정 모델)
Epigenetics???

  Epigenetics는 DNA 서열의 변화 없이 유전 가능한 유전자의 발현 (expression) 이나 형질 (phenotype) 의 변화를 일으키는 모든 기작을 말한다. 이는 DNA의 methylation과 같은 DNA modification, DNA와 histone의 결합 위치를 변화시키는 chromatin remodeling, histone modification의 변화 등을 통하여 일어난다.

그림 1. epigenetic regulation 의 종류. Zhou el al., Nat Rev Genet., 2011

Epigenetics의 중요성 및 식물 epigenetics 연구의 장점

  이러한 epigenetics, 특히 DNA methylation은 식물의 발달 및 개화 뿐 아니라 동물에서의 발달, 암 형성, 기억, 면역 반응 등 생장과 발달에 필수적인 다양한 현상을 조절하는 것으로 알려져 있다.

제출

AP Feinberg et al. 2005 Nat. Rev. Gen.

그림 2. 환경의 변화 및 식습관의 변화가 epigenetic change를 일으켜 유전자의 발현이 변화하면 이로 인해 oncogene (ONC) 나 tumor suppressor gene (TSG), gate keeper mutation (GKM) 이 유도되어 암 발생으로 이어진다

  그러나 동물에서 이러한 DNA methylation을 연구하는데는 많은 제약이 따른다. 우선 대부분의 DNA methylation 관련 돌연변이체가 성체로 생존하지 못하고, C. elegans나 yeast의 경우에는 DNA methylation이 일어나지 않는다. 그러나 식물의 경우 동물과 비슷한 DNA methylation기작을 가지고 있으면서 이들의 돌연변이체가 온전히 한 세대를 보낼수 있기 때문에 돌연변이체의 구축 및 유지가 가능하다. 따라서 식물에서의 epigenetics 연구는 식물의 생장 및 발달 뿐 아니라 이를 응용하여 동물에서의 epigenetics 기작 연구에도 응용 가능하다는 점에서 큰 장점을 가지고 있다.

Epigenetics 를 넘어 epigenomics로

  DNA tiling microarray 와 같은 기술의 개발에 따라 DNA methylation 및 histone modification의 변화를 게놈 전체 수준에서 측정하고 연구할 수 있는 epigenomics의 시대가 열렸다. 여기서 한발 더 나아가 최근에는  DNA bisulfite sequencing, next generation sequencing 등을 통하여 게놈 전체의 methyl cytosine의 위치를 정확히 동정하는것이 가능해졌다. 이에 따라 Arabidopsis의 발달 과정에 따른 DNA methylation의 변화나 여러 DNA methyltransferase 돌연변이체에서의 DNA methylation 변화에 관한 보고가 이루어지고 있다.

 제출

그림 3. 본 실험실에서는 다양한 epigenetic regulator의 돌연변이체에서의 stress 저항성 확인을 통하여 biotic / abiotic stress 저항성을 변화시키는 epigenetic regulator를 동정하고 whole genome bisulfite sequencing과 microarray를 통하여 그 target gene과 조절 기작을 규명하고 있다.

  본 실험실은 Next generation sequencing 을 통하여 게놈 전체 수준에서 DNA methylation 및 이에 따른 유전자 발현의 변화를 관찰할 수 있는 시스템을 갖추고 있다. 이를 통하여 식물의 내제된 생장 및 발달 프로그램 뿐 아니라 병 저항성, 스트레스 저항성과 같은 환경 자극에 의해 일어나는 빠른 신호 전달 과정에서도 DNA methylation과 같은 epigenetic 조절이 매우 중요한 역할을 하고 있음을 밝혀내고 있다

Cytokinin 신호 조절을 통한 높은 생산성과 병저항성을 지니는 작물 개발

 Cytokinin은 식물 줄기세포의 분열을 촉진시켜 생장을 빠르게 하고 작물의 생산성을 증가시킨다. 최근 벼에서 cytokinin에 의해 직접적으로 쌀의 생산량이 증가되는 것이 확인되었다. 또한 cytokinin은 세포 내의 활성 산소 증가를 억제함으로서 가뭄과 같은 스트레스에 대한 저항성을 증가시키는 것으로 알려져 있다. 그러나 식물에 의해 생산되는 cytokinin이 식물의 병 저항성에 어떠한 영향을 주는 지는 아직 알려진 바가 없다. 본 연구실에서는 cytokinin을 분비하지 않는 병원균과 cytokinin signaling 돌연변이체를 사용하여 병저항성에 미치는 cytokinin을 확인해 본 결과 놀랍게도 cytokinin이 병저항성을 증가시킨다는 것을 확인하였다.

 제출
그림 1. Cytokinin에 의한 병저항성 증가 기작. Cytokinin이 풍부한 줄기세포 부분에서는 cytokinin에 의해 ARR2와 같은 전사 조절 인자가 활성화 된다. ARR2는 병저항성을 조절하는 핵심 호르몬인 salicylic acid 전사 조절 인자인 TGA3와 결합하여 TGA3에 의한 병저항성 유전자 발현을 증가시킴으로서 병원균에 대한 저항성을 조절한다.

Stomatal immunity 조절을 통한 병저항성

Stomata 는 공기의 출입통로임과 동시에 병원균이 식물로 침입하는 통로이기도 하다. 따라서 stomata 의 개폐를 통한 stomatal immunity는 병저항성에 중요한 역할을 한다. salicylic acid (SA) 나 abscisic acid (ABA) 에 의한 stomatal immunity 조절에 관한 연구는 보고되었지만, 식물생장을 촉진시키는 호르몬인 cytokinin 에 의한 stomatal immunity 조절에 관한 연구는 보고된 바 없다. 본 실험실에서는 cytokinin 에 의한 stomatal immunity 조절기작을 확인하였다. 이를 통해 식물생장 촉진과 높은 병저항성을 동시에 가질 수 있는 기작에 대한 연구를 진행하고 있다.

Phytohormone network
식물 발달 과정에 있어서 Brassinosteroid의 역할 및 다른 호르몬과의 상호작용

 식물의 유일한 스테로이드 호르몬인 brassinosteroid는 주로 세포의 길이생장과 줄기의 성장에 관여하고 있는 것으로 알려져 있었다. 최근 식물의 일생에 가장 중요하게 작용하는 빛에 의한 생장과 발달(photomorphogenesis)의 조절에도 중요하게 작용하고 있음이 밝혀져 이 분야에 대한 연구가 활발하게 이루어지고 있다. 최근 brassinosteroid의 신호전달 연구에서 작물의 생산성이나 biomass의 증산에 매우 중요하게 관여하고 있음 또한 알려져, 앞으로 인류가 해결해 나가야 할 식량난이나 대체에너지 개발에 필요한 고 생산성 식물 개발에 매우 유용하게 이용될 것으로 기대되고 있는 신호전달 연구분야이다.

그림1. brassinosteroid 신호전달 돌연변이체의 특이적인 난쟁이 표현형 (Li et al., 2001)과 신호전달 모델 (Ryu et al., 2007)

 Brassinosteroid 신호전달에 관여하는 중요한 인산화 효소인 BIN2라는 단백질은 brassinosteroid 신호전달에 있어서 중요한 전사인자인 BES1, BZR1의 시 공간적 분포를 조절함으로써 신호의 강도를 조절하는 인자이다. 흥미롭게도 이 인산화 효소는 auxin이라는 식물의 발달과정에 있어서 매우 중요한 호르몬의 신호전달 경로에 관여하고 있다는 사실을 본 연구실에서 알아내었다. 특이적으로 auxin에 의해 매개되는 유전자 발현을 담당하는 전사인자인 ARF들의 인산화 상태를 조절함을 알아내었고 이를 통한 식물의 곁뿌리 형성에 있어서 인산화 효소의 역할을 규명하였다. 본 연구실은 이러한 관찰을 바탕으로 두 호르몬의 식물 발달과정에서의 상호작용을 알아내고 이를 바탕으로 식물의 형태형성을 심도 있게 이해하기 위하여 다양한 유전학적 생화학적 기법을 사용하여 연구를 진행하고 있다.

그림 2. auxin 의존적인 곁뿌리 발달에서 brassinosteroid 신호 전달에 중요한 인산화 효소 돌연변이체의 곁뿌리 발달 형성 증가

 Cytokinin과 Glutamate에 의한 콩과식물에서의 뿌리혹 생성의 신호전달 체계 확립

  현재의 인류 사회는 산업화 이후 기하 급수적인 인구증가로 인해 전통적인 농업으로는 식량의 생산성의 한계에 직면하였었다. 하지만 녹색 혁명 이후 식량의 생산량이 증가하여 식량문제의 해결을 앞당겼지만 작물의 생장을 위한 기본적인 토양의 능력은 한계에 직면하였고 이를 해결하기 위한 수많은 비료의 사용이 불가피 하였다. 특히 질소 비료의 생산에 있어서 Bosch와 Haber가 개발한 인공 질소 생산 방법은 비료의 개발에 있어서 획기적인 전환점이었지만 생산에 많은 에너지와 비용이 들어가며 석유가격에 대한 의존성 때문에 비료의 생산가격 또한 점점 증가하는 추세이다. 하지만 이렇게 많은 양의 인공 질소 비료 생산에도 불구하고 자연계에 존재하는 콩과 식물의 질소고정 양의 절반에도 미치지 못하는 상황이다.

그림 3. 미국에서 질소 비료 생산량과 질소 비료 생산단가 변화

인공 질소 비료의 과다사용으로 토양의 산성화와 해양의 부영양화가 심각한 환경문제로 대두 되고 있으며 토질의 저하로 인한 작물의 생산량 감소, 이를 극복하기 위한 과량의 비료의 사용이라는 악순환을 반복하고 있는 현 농업의 상황은 자연적인 질소 고정, 특히 콩과 식물의 뿌리혹에 의한 질소고정 연구가 얼마나 중요한 것인지를 보여주는 것이라 할 수 있다.

그림 4. 질소 비료 과다 사용에 의한 토양의 산성화와 부영양화

  최근에 보고된 일련의 연구결과에서 콩과 식물에서 cytokinin을 인지하는 유전자에 돌연변이가 생긴 경우 질소 고정균 없이도 질소 고정을 할 수 있는 기관을 형성한다는 것을 보고하였고 이는 뿌리혹 형성에 있어서 cytokinin의 신호전달이 매우 중요하게 작용하고 있다는 것을 알 수 있다. 특히 cytokinin 신호전달 체계는 콩과 식물 뿐 아니라 모든 식물이 공통적으로 가지고 있으며 질소고정균과의 특이적인 상호작용을 통해 뿌리 혹 형성을 유도한다는 사실은 식물 종에 상관없이 뿌리혹 생성을 연구하는데 아주 중요한 일이 될 것이다.

그림 5. 질소 고정균 없이 뿌리혹 생성을 하는 cytokinin 수용체 돌연변이( Trichine et al., 2007)

  본 연구실에서는 cytokinin보다 상위의 신호전달 체계로서 glutamate가 신호전달물질로 작동하는 것을 관찰하였으며 glutamate 역시 뿌리 혹 형성을 조절하고 있다는 사실을 관찰하였고 이를 바탕으로 질소고정에 있어 새로운 신호전달 체제를 탐색, 새로운 유전자를 발굴하고 이를 통하여 질소고정의 효율을 증가시키는 방법, 다른 중요한 작물에서 자발적인 질소 고정을 통해 ‘fertilizer free’ 농업 기술을 획득하는 것을 목표로 연구를 진행하고 있다.

Plant DB - 식물 생장에 중요한 호르몬과 환경요인 사이의 상호작용 연구를 위한 리소스 제공

  식물 호르몬은 식물의 생장을 조절하는 작은 화합물로, abscisic acid, auxin, cytokinin, jasmonate, salicyclic acid, brassinosteroid, gibberellins, ethylene, strigolactone 등 9가지 주요 호르몬이 존재하는 것으로 알려져 있다. 각 호르몬은 생성 및 저장되는 조직이 서로 다르며, 호르몬이 활성화되는 신호 또한 각기 다양하다. 호르몬과 더불어 식물 생장에 중요한 영향을 미치는 요인은 빛 (파장, 세기), 온도, 습도, 토양의 수분 및 염도 등을 포함한 비생물학적 환경 요인 (abiotic stress) 과 병원성 균 혹은 공생 균 등에 의한 생물학적 환경 요인 (biotic stress) 이 있다. 과연 이러한 환경적 요인과 식물 호르몬은 어떠한 방식으로 상호작용을 함으로써 식물의 생장을 조절하는 것일까?

그림 6. 식물 생장 호르몬과 환경적 요인 사이의 상호작용

  식물 호르몬과 비생물학적, 생물학적 환경 요인의 상호작용은 식물학자들의 주된 연구 주제였으며, 분자 유전학적인 접근 방법을 통한 연구가 활발히 이루어져 왔다. 여기서 우리는 PlantDB를 통해 식물 생장과 관련된 호르몬 및 환경 요인의 상호작용 연구에 도움이 될 수 있는 리소스를 제공하고자 한다. 20가지 이상의 호르몬, 비생물학적, 생물학적 환경요인에 대한 Arabidopsis에서의 microarray data를 분석하였고, 식물 호르몬 신호 전달에 중요한 유전자 사이의 상호작용을 500여개의 publication으로 부터 정리하였다. PlantDB에서 제공하고 있는 웹 기반의 분석 툴은 다양한 조건 속에서 Venn diagram으로부터 원하는 유전자 군을 선별하는 것을 시작으로, expression pattern에 따른 세부적인 유전자 군 발굴, core modulator 발굴, network visualization 등의 일련의 과정을 하나의 프레임 웍으로 통합함으로써, 관심 있는 생장 조건과 관련된 data로부터 core network의 추출을 가능케 하고 있다. 이렇게 통합된 하나의 프레임 웍은 transcriptome, interactome 을 이용해 아직 밝혀지지 않은 생장 요인 사이의 상호작용에 관한 data-driven hypothesis를 설립하는 데에 도움을 줄 것으로 기대된다. PlantDB는 현재 구축 중에 있으며, 앞으로 본 홈페이지 상단 메뉴의 DATABASE 링크를 통해 서비스가 제공될 것이다.

그림 7. 호르몬 - 환경요인 간 상호작용 연구를 위한 transcriptome, interactome 및 data 분석을 위한 웹기반의 툴의 통합된 리소스 제공

intro.text:
Our Research
Our research goal is to advance the state of the art in emerging large-scale system platforms by making them more efficient, responsive, intelligent, and programmable. Our current research topics lie in the following areas, and continues to evolve as new challenges emerge:

Efficient LLM Serving Systems
: We design inference and serving systems that meet strict latency and cost targets at production scale.

Continual and On-Device Learning
: We build methods and system support for continual adaptation on resource-constrained devices and edge environments.

Large-Scale Distributed Training
: We develop techniques to train models efficiently across heterogeneous and geo-distributed clusters.

Fast and Scalable Big Data Analytics
: We build data systems that accelerate iterative analytics and scalable ML data pipelines.

OUR MAIN RESEARCH
RESEARCH DETAILS ⚠
FAST DISTRIBUTED TRAINING ON HETEROGENEOUS ACCELERATORS
Fast distributed training on heterogeneous accelerators is a technique to speed up AI model training by efficiently combining different types of hardware (e.g., NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and specialized TPUs) into a single, cohesive system.
EFFICIENT CACHING FOR ITERATIVE ANALYTICS
Efficient caching for iterative analytics is a strategy designed to speed up data-heavy tasks—like machine learning training or big data queries—by intelligently storing and reusing data that is accessed repeatedly.
DATA PREPROCESSING FOR SCALABLE ML PIPELINES
Data preprocessing for scalable ML pipelines is the process of transforming raw data into a clean, usable format at a scale that can handle millions or billions of records without crashing the system.
SLO-AWARE, ADAPTIVE KV CACHE MANAGEMENT
SLO-aware, adaptive KV cache management is a system-level optimization for Large Language Model (LLM) serving that dynamically balances memory usage and performance to meet specific Service Level Objectives (SLOs), such as Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) or Time-Between-Tokens (TBT).
GENERALIZED KV CACHE REUSE
Generalized KV Cache Reuse is an advanced optimization for LLM serving that allows the system to reuse KV cache segments from any part of a prompt, moving beyond the limitations of traditional prefix caching.
ACCURACY-PRESERVING LONG-CONTEXT PRUNING
Accuracy-preserving long-context pruning is a technique used to compress the KV cache of Large Language Models (LLMs) by removing less important tokens without degrading the model's performance on long-context tasks.
SLO-AWARE FAILURE RECOVERY FOR LLMS
SLO-aware failure recovery for LLMs is a resilience strategy designed to recover from hardware or software failures while strictly minimizing the impact on Service Level Objectives (SLOs) like latency and throughput.
SYSTEMS FOR AGENTIC AI
Systems for Agentic AI are specialized software architectures designed to support AI agents that don't just "chat," but independently plan, use tools, and execute multi-step tasks to achieve a goal.
LOW-LATENCY, HIGH-ACCURACY ON-DEVICE LEARNING
Low-latency, high-accuracy on-device learning refers to the ability of a local device (like a smartphone, IoT sensor, or medical device) to train and adapt its AI models instantly without relying on cloud servers.
ADAPTIVE, RESOURCE-EFFICIENT CONTINUAL LEARNING
Adaptive, resource-efficient continual learning is an AI paradigm that allows models to learn from a constant stream of new data while operating within the strict physical limits of local hardware (like smartphones or IoT sensors).
LEARNING-BASED PLANNING FOR HETEROGENEOUS, GEO-DISTRIBUTED TRAINING
Learning-based planning for heterogeneous, geo-distributed training is an intelligent orchestration strategy used to train large AI models across multiple, physically separated data centers with varying hardware capabilities.

intro.text:
Home > Research Area
In CSP laboratory, we conduct the research on various topics. Each topics share the fundamental idea of advanced solidification concepts. Based on this theory, our lab strives to understand and study the solidification behavior of materials widely used in industrial fields such as nuclear power plant and steel making company. Research criteria are followed as 5 parts:
Controlling Solidification Structures of Cast Materials
Cu-Fe alloy is a typical alloy system in which phase separation occurs in the liquid state due to its positive enthalpy and wide solid-liquid coexistence region. When the austenitic phase nucleation occurs earlier than liquid phase separation during the solidification process, the liquid phase separation behavior can be controlled. Based on these facts, the optimal inoculant element for Copper-Ferrous alloy and medium entropy alloy (MEA) composition could be found from using thermodynamical calculations, and the process of phase transformation. Texture and microstructural analysis are considering the specimen produced with vibration technical casting machine (VTC) and analyzed with differential scanning calorimeter (DSC).
<1. Controlling Solidification Structures of Cast Materials>
Thermo-physical properties of oxide glasses and mold fluxes
In order to understand atomic-scale structure in a multi-oxide glass in a detail, it is necessary to control its physical and chemical properties. Especially “Borosilicate glass” has been adopted for various usage, including matrices for immobilization of high-level radioactive nuclear waste, mold fluxes for continuous casting of high Al-steels, and sealing materials for solid oxide fuel cells. By using complementary tools such as solid-state magic-angle spinning (MAS) NMR, vibrational spectroscopy, XAFS, and molecular dynamics (MD) for structural analysis of glass.
Furthermore, controlling the heat transfer and providing lubrication in a casting mold is the most essential in conventional casting process. These following functions will govern by various physical properties of mold flux, such as thermal conductivity and viscosity which is desirable to understand both the structure and properties. Heat transfer phenomena in casting mold strongly depends on the crystallization behaviors of mold flux such as melting crystallization kinetics and morphological evolution of crystalline phase.
Thus, we are aiming on fundamental but extremely relevant studies on thermo-physical properties of multi-oxide glasses and mold fluxes. Development of advanced multi oxide glass systems topics can be conclude as follow:
1) Structural Elucidation of Mixed Ion Effect in Oxide Glasses
2) Effect of Li2O on CaO-SiO2-CaF2-based Mold Flux
3) Heat Transfer control by dispersed metallic particles in glassy mold flux
4) Increase Mo solubility in Mo glass by structural stabilization.
<2. Thermo-physical properties of oxide glasses and mold fluxes>
Additive manufacturing process
Additive Manufacturing (AM) process also known as 3D printing is a construction of 3D model by specifying single layer of material transported from 3d CAD file. The 3D bulk specimen manufactured by AM is being applied in various fields of industry due to its finer microstructure and superior mechanical properties than that of the conventional casting process. The analysis on chemical metallurgy-based metal AM research starts from understanding microstructural changes based on the advanced solidification theory.
For our research scope, we use both powder bed fusion type printer and direct energy deposition type to observe the microstructural tendency, application method and strengthening mechanism by formation behavior of inclusions such as nitride and oxide.
In addition, we are exploring the strengthening effect and thermodynamical analysis of inclusions and precipitates generated during rapid solidification through controlling the cooling rate and shielding gas flow rate.
Furthermore, our group focuses on various experiments such as controlling the difference in solidification behavior between heterojunctions functionally graded material and analyzing microstructural changes by simulation method and thermodynamical calculations.
<3. Additive manufacturing process>
Radioactive waste management
There are various types of radionuclides in nuclear fuel waste that must be disposed safely and isolated from the human society. In order to separate radionuclides from nuclear fuel waste, nuclear waste recycling process like ‘pyro process’ is performed, which leads separation of radionuclides such as radioactive rare earth, Technetium (Tc), Iodine (I), Cesium (Cs) and Strontium (Sr).
Hazardous radionuclides immobilized into a glass form (vitrification process) and disposed underground, efficiency in terms of volume reduction with chemical stability could achieve that is possible to alleviate social and economic burden by reducing the size of the repository site.
In our laboratory, we are conducting research such as the development of a glass solidified material capable of carrying radionuclides for a long-term period, and the investigation of their radiation effects, physical stability, and glass structure by using analysis methods such as XRF, NMR, Raman, and EXAFS.
Computational Material Science
Material’s property could be varied from the compositional and structural changes of material. Conventional experimental method has been reported as erroneous method which is time consuming with repetitive trials to find the ultimate calculation.
Our research group majorly performs Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation, Machine Learning (ML), Finite Element Method (FEM), Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo Simulation (MC) to figure metal material with glass ceramic materials’ mechanical property and chemically stable structural composition analysis.
<5. Computational Material Science>

연구 주제
식물병리학의 병삼각형 (Disease triangle)은 기주식물, 병원체와 더불어 환경적인 요인이 식물병의 발생에서 중요한 요소라는 것을 강조하고 있습니다. 그러나 이전의 분자식물병리학 연구들은 기주식물과 병원체의 상호작용에 초점을 맞추어 진행되었고, 그렇기 때문에 식물-미생물 상호작용에서 환경이 주는 변화에 대한 연구가 필요합니다. 특히 변화하는 기후로 인하여 식물병이 증가하고 있는 상황에서 우리 연구실은 식물-미생물 상호작용 속 분자적 변화를 이해하여 이를 극복할 수 있는 방안을 연구합니다.
모델 식물인 애기장대를 넘어 유전자 교정 기법을 통한 저온 작물의 기후탄력적 면역설계 방법을 연구합니다.
Research interest II
Can we engineer host plants for the production of pharmaceutical proteins?
연구 주제

Supporting:
Environmental effects on plant-pathogen interaction - Dr. Sheng Yang He's lab, Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Michigan State University/Duke University (2018 - 2023)
A long-standing dogma in plant disease susceptibility states that disease development requires not only the presence of a virulent pathogen and a susceptible host but also a set of disease-favoring environmental conditions. How environmental conditions influence the plant and the pathogen during an active interaction is poorly understood, leaving a big gap in our understanding of how disease outbreaks occur in nature. To gain insight into the molecular basis of the “disease triangle” dogma, we initiated a project aimed at elucidating how two prominent abiotic environmental factors (temperature and humidity) intercept the molecular network associated with disease development.
Small proteins modulate ion channel-like ACD6 to regulate immunity in Arabidopsis thaliana
In this project, we studied the precise biochemical mechanism by which ACD6 and related proteins in plants act remains enigmatic. Several lines of evidence link increased ACD6 activity to enhanced calcium influx, likely mediated by ACD6 itself and with MHA1L as a direct regulator of ACD6. (Chen, Li, Kim, Neuhäuser et al. 2023)

In this project, we studied how elevated (suboptimal) temperature affects plant immunity and report rate-limiting genes to build temperature-resilient immunity. (Kim and Castroverde et al. 2022)
Crops of the future: building a climate-resilient plant immune system
In this review paper, we discussed how environmental condition affects plant immunity and how to build climate-resilient plant immunity. (Kim and Hilleary et al., 2021).
Plant defense responses against abiotic stresses - Dr. Woo Taek Kim's Lab, Yonsei University (2010 – 2018)
Plants receive diverse stimuli from the environment over their life and reprogram their transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome to acquire better. These responses are quickly and tightly regulated by the environment. 10 % of the Arabidopsis genome is predicted to be dedicated to encoding genes that are involved in the Ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), the major protease complex in higher organisms, suggesting that the UPS plays a crucial role in dynamically regulating the proteome in response to given stimuli. As an identifier of substrates in the UPS, E3 Ub ligases are essential to building a complex network among the UPS and its diverse substrates. During my Ph.D. course, I focused on elucidating physiological and molecular functions of RING E3 Ub ligase genes which are involved in plant defense mechanisms against abiotic stresses, such as drought and high salinity, using the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana.
Identification of Arabidopsis RING E3 Ubiquitin (Ub) ligase AtAIRP3/LOG2, which is a positive regulator in plant defense responses against high-salt and drought stress
Through a reverse genetic screen, we found that AtAIRP3/LOG2 is a positive regulator in ABA-mediated defense responses against high salinity and drought stress (Kim and Kim, 2013).
Characterization of molecular mechanisms under the function of RING ligase AtAIRP2
We identified ATP1/SDIRIP1, an interacting partner of the RING E3 ligase AtAIRP2, which is positive regulator of ABA-mediated drought responses. Through genetic and molecular approaches, it is revealed that the physiological function of AtAIRP2 is dependent on ATP1/SDIRIP1 and the half-life of ATP1/SDIRIP1 is negatively affected by AtAIRP2; this suggests that AtAIRP2 functions through regulating half-life of ATP1/SDIRIP1 in response to ABA (Oh and Kim et al., 2017).
Characterization of plant defense responses against proteotoxic stress in higher plant
While studying RING E3 ligases on ABA-mediated stress responses, we found that abiotic stresses, such as drought and heat, induce protein damage. We screened RING E3 ligases which are involved in defense response against protein damaging stress and identified MPSR1. The MPSR1 protein functions as a quick surveillance system to monitor for damaged proteins and maintains proteasome activity under protein damaging stress for protein quality control (Kim et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2019).
Identification of microtubule-localized RING E3 ligase AtJUL1, which is involved in ABA-mediated stomatal regulation
Through a reverse genetic screen, we identified AtJUL1, which is a positive regulator in ABA-mediated stomatal regulation and defense mechanism against drought stress. AtJUL1 is localized to cortical microtubule through direct interaction with microtubule bundle and involved in catastrophe of cortical microtubule in guard cell, which is one of the essential steps to close stomata in response to drought (Yu et al., 2020).

intro.text:
Our research broadly lies in statistics and data science. We aim to develop principled statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional and complex data, along with foundational theories to understand and justify these methods. Our interests span both methodological development and theoretical analysis, often guided by practical challenges arising in real-world applications.
Some of our current research directions include:
Statistical perspectives on deep learning
Distributionally robust inference
Bayesian online learning and domain adaptation
Frequentist theory for Bayesian procedures
We strive to maintain a balance between theoretical and applied research. Much of our applied work is driven by collaborations with researchers in both academia and industry. Below are a few notable recent collaborations:
Collaboration with Seungho Song: We are collaborating with Professor Seungho Song, a colorectal surgeon at Kyungpook National University School of Medicine, to model the risk of postoperative complications following colorectal cancer surgery. A key aspect of this project is leveraging datasets from different domains, such as surgical data from Korea and Japan, to enable effective modeling even in regions with limited data. The goal is to build robust and generalizable models that can support clinical decision-making in diverse healthcare settings.
Collaboration with Yogiyo and Dong Gu Choi: South Korea’s food delivery industry has experienced rapid growth over the past decade, presenting a range of interesting data science challenges. We collaborated with Yogiyo, one of the country’s largest food delivery companies, to address some of these problems. Our main focus was on predicting demand for food delivery, with the goal of informing the dynamic pricing of rider commissions. The collaboration itself was also featured in media coverage.
Collaboration with Samsung C&T and Minseok Song: We collaborated with Samsung C&T to develop a fashion recommendation system for SSF Shop. The project involved utilizing various data sources, including customer click history, product images, and a curated set of compatible fashion items collected by domain experts. The collaboration was also featured in media coverage.
